evidence.activity: OCBC SeniorCare programme supporting seniors' health, wealth, literacy and lifestyle needs
evidence.quote: With over $2 million invested to support more than 180,000 seniors, the programme helps seniors manage their health, wealth, literacy and lifestyle needs with confidence.
evidence.section: Annual report > Group CEO statement > Investing in People, Communities and Sustainability

community.criterion: level 3: named external education/community program with dollars and participants

evidence.activity: Dialect-speaking branch ambassadors for seniors and accessible app text resizing
evidence.quote: We introduced OCBC CARE Ambassadors in selected branches to assist seniors in familiar dialects and enhanced digital accessibility with smart text resizing on the OCBC mobile app.
evidence.section: Annual report > Group CEO statement > Investing in People, Communities and Sustainability

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: multilingual/dialect service and accessibility feature, limited reach disclosed

evidence.activity: Pay-to-wallet remittance feature aimed at the unbanked and Singapore's foreign workforce
evidence.quote: Expanded the OCBC app’s pay-to-wallet feature to cover 10 leading digital wallets across Asia, improving remittance speed, cost and accessibility especially for the region’s unbanked population and Singapore’s foreign workforce
evidence.section: Annual report > 2025 Sustainability Highlights > Bringing Impact to Communities

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: service built for immigrant workers and underserved customers, reach not disclosed

evidence.activity: OCBC-SDSC SwimTogether water safety programme for persons with disabilities, fully funded by OCBC
evidence.quote: Fully funded by OCBC, the programme supports 100 participants across 800 classes led by trained coaches and OCBC staff volunteers.
evidence.section: Annual report > Helping Where it Matters > Singapore > OCBC-SDSC SwimTogether Programme

cross_cultural.criterion: level 3: named accessibility/inclusion program for persons with disabilities with participant numbers

community.criterion: level 2-3: funded community program with participant numbers
level 3: volunteering with measured volunteers, hours and people reached

evidence.activity: OCBC Ignite early talent programme for polytechnic students
evidence.quote: Since the launch of OCBC Ignite in 2024, we have welcomed more than 300 students across all 5 local polytechnics into the programme, further contributing to the goal of boosting participation of polytechnic graduates in the financial sector in Singapore.
evidence.section: Annual report > Our People > Early talent pathways

community.criterion: level 3: named external education program with participant numbers

evidence.activity: Five-year tuition programme for underprivileged children at The Hut Singapore
evidence.quote: A five year tuition programme was introduced for underprivileged children at The Hut Singapore, providing them with long-term, sustained academic support.
evidence.section: Annual report > Bringing Impact to Communities

community.criterion: level 2: specific external education program, reach not disclosed

evidence.activity: Ramadan food package distribution to families in need in Indonesia
evidence.quote: In celebration of OCBC Indonesia’s 84th anniversary and the month of Ramadan, the teams in Indonesia and OCBC Syariah distributed 1,000 food packages to families in need across Jakarta, Banten, and West Java.
evidence.section: Annual report > Helping Where it Matters > Indonesia > Ramadan Food Distribution

community.criterion: level 2: specific community activity, limited reach

evidence.activity: Branch-funded medical equipment donation for rural communities in Malaysia
evidence.quote: Together with Klinik Kesihatan Bukit Pelandok in Port Dickson, the OCBC Seremban branch funded RM19,352 worth of essential medical equipment to strengthen healthcare services for rural communities.
evidence.section: Annual report > Helping Where it Matters > Malaysia > OCBC Seremban medical equipment donation

community.criterion: level 2: specific community investment, limited reach

evidence.activity: Coaching for Growth programme with ICF-trained internal coaches
evidence.quote: As of December 2025, our community of 52 ICF-trained coaches has inspired and guided more than 300 employees, empowering them to grow with confidence and unlock their fullest personal and professional potential.

evidence.activity: AI, Digital and Data training for employees
evidence.quote: In the past three years, around three in five employees have participated in training programmes related to AI, Digital and Data.
evidence.section: Annual report > Tech Shift > Workforce capabilities

evidence.activity: Cyber Certification Pathway 2.0 upskilling employees into cybersecurity roles
evidence.quote: Over 200 graduates from key markets including Singapore, Malaysia, Mainland China and Hong Kong have completed the programme
evidence.section: Annual report > 2025 Sustainability Highlights > Conducting Our Business Responsibly

evidence.activity: 'Life in a Snapshot' photography and storytelling programme for seniors with dementia, ending in a public artwork showcase
evidence.quote: OCBC volunteers delved into in-depth conversations with the seniors and continued to engage them over six months to hold a public showcase featuring artwork reflecting stories from their lives.
evidence.section: Annual report > Helping Where it Matters > Hong Kong > Life in a Snapshot

creativity.criterion: level 2: single small arts/storytelling community program, limited reach

evidence.activity: Women Unlimited programme supporting women entrepreneurs across four markets
evidence.quote: Our Women Unlimited programme now extends across Singapore, Indonesia, Hong Kong and Malaysia, with a goal to support 10,000 women entrepreneurs by 2030.
evidence.section: Annual report > Group CEO statement > SME programmes
evidence.indicators: 10,000 women entrepreneurs by 2030 (target, not achieved reach)

entrepreneurship.criterion: level 2: named program for underserved founders; reach to date not disclosed

evidence.activity: Serial Entrepreneur programme supporting founders of multiple small businesses
evidence.quote: The Serial Entrepreneur programme, which supports founders who own multiple small businesses, was also expanded in 2025 across our core markets.
evidence.section: Annual report > Group CEO statement > SME programmes

entrepreneurship.criterion: level 2: named founder program, reach not disclosed

evidence.activity: OCBC SME Start-ESG Programme giving SMEs grant-funded assessment, expert advice and loan access
evidence.quote: The Programme helps SMEs obtain a baseline measurement of their sustainability metrics with a grant from EnterpriseSG, expert advice on sustainability practices and access to sustainability-linked loans (SLLs) from OCBC.
evidence.section: Annual report > Global Commercial Banking > Supporting SMEs

entrepreneurship.criterion: level 2: named advisory/grant-supported SME program, reach not disclosed

evidence.activity: Singpass authentication to ease cross-border business account opening
evidence.quote: To reduce friction for cross-border business formation, we became the first bank to enable Singpass authentication for Singaporeans opening business accounts in Malaysia.
evidence.section: Annual report > Global Commercial Banking > Johor

entrepreneurship.criterion: level 2: tool reducing barriers to business formation, reach not disclosed

creativity.reason: Level 2: the core business is banking with no creative activity, and the only specific creative activity is one small arts/storytelling community programme.

community.reason: Level 3: external education and community investment with substantial measured reach (SeniorCare over $2 million and 180,000 seniors, Ignite 300+ students, 17,681 volunteers), but not shown to be central to strategy at level 4 scale.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 3: a named inclusion programme for persons with disabilities with participant figures, plus customer-access services for seniors, the unbanked and foreign workers; access is not shown as a major measured business line.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 2: several named enabling programmes for founders and SMEs, but no disclosed count of businesses actually helped (the 10,000 figure is a 2030 target).

ai.notes: OCBC SeniorCare is cited once for Community (E1): the report gives 'more than 180,000 seniors' (framed elsewhere as over three years) and separately 'more than 100,000 seniors' reached to date, so the 180,000 figure may be a multi-year target. The Women Unlimited 10,000 figure is a 2030 goal and was not treated as current reach. Total donations of $3.87m (65% community) appear in a stats panel without a quotable sentence and were not used as an indicator. The Marriott partnership supporting 12,000 SME suppliers with working capital was treated as ordinary SME financing (serving) and not scored. The Punggol Digital District presence is planned. Board gender-diversity targets are governance disclosures and were not scored. Required cyber security training was excluded as compliance training. The creativity level 2 rests on one small programme; a reviewer may view it as level 1.
